title: Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation (Buffer pH)

references.label: General microbiology/quantitative methods references (ASM, FDA BAM)

explanation: Relates the pH of a buffer solution to the ratio of its conjugate base ([A-], the deprotonated form) to its weak acid ([HA], the protonated form) and the acid's dissociation constant (pKa). It is the basis for calculating how much of a weak acid and its conjugate base to combine to reach a target buffer pH, and for predicting how a buffer's pH shifts as that ratio changes.

variables.meaning: Target or resulting pH of the buffer solution
Negative log10 of the acid dissociation constant for the specific weak acid/base pair in use
Molar concentration of the conjugate base form
Molar concentration of the weak acid form

workedExample.scenario: Preparing an acetate buffer using acetic acid (pKa ≈ 4.76) where the conjugate base concentration is twice the weak acid concentration ([A-]/[HA] = 2).

commonMistakes: Using a pKa value measured at a different temperature or ionic strength than the actual buffer conditions without accounting for the difference.
Applying the equation far outside the buffer's effective range (roughly pKa ± 1), where buffering capacity is weak and the approximation becomes less reliable in practice.
Confusing the ratio direction — mixing up [A-]/[HA] with [HA]/[A-] flips the sign of the log term.
